newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev closes firmer near 2,900 per dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev closes firmer near 2,900 per dollar.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev advanced to around 2,900 per dollar at close from 3,020-3,050 at the opening as dollar supply topped demand and was expected to firm further next week, dealers said.
"Banks and clients sold dollars for levs they needed for pending payments while a general lev shortage prevented big final clients from buying large volumes," one dealer said.
Some dealers attributed the increased dollar supply from banks to the fact that next week banks are to pay their minimum required reserves for January at the central bank.
"But volumes on offer would hardly be so large as to trigger a rapid lev rebound," another dealer said.
The lev traded near 3,100 at the beginning of the week.

News of International Monetary Fund (IMF) missions arriving this month to resume talks on introduction of a fixed exchange rate regime, the currency board system, would probably support the lev next week, traders said.
"The lev may firm further or at least trade range bound at 2,800-3,000 next week while talks with the mission are under way," said a dealer.

Two International Monetary Fund teams are due in Bulgaria in the middle of next week and on February 24 to resume talks on implementation of a currency board system aimed at hauling the country back from the brink of default, officials said. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
